checks.statement: The navigation rail should be placed vertically along the leading edge of the window.
checks.condition: When integrating a navigation rail: left for LTR content, right for RTL content.

sourceHistory.summary: Record the captured Container instruction without importing the exploratory audit assessments.
Preserve the source’s should recommendation rather than an unconditional imperative; confirm provenance against extractor version 2.

evidence.result: The rail surface occupies the first inline flex slot; modal placement uses inset-inline-start:0, which follows LTR/RTL direction.

implementation.notes: The rail is placed at the logical leading edge, including in its modal layout.

checks.statement: Always put the rail in the same place across screens of an app.
checks.condition: When the app uses a navigation rail.

evidence.result: The standalone specimen has no app-level integration context for this exact condition: “When the app uses a navigation rail.”.

implementation.notes: The source says “Always put the rail in the same place across screens of an app.” under “When the app uses a navigation rail.”. This condition concerns destination hierarchy, app layout, product choice, or a screen transition that the isolated navigation-rail specimen does not own. This disposition applies only to that integration condition.

checks.statement: The rail should contain 3–7 destinations, with an optional FAB.
checks.condition: When configuring primary rail destinations.
checks.notes: The guidelines apply the count specifically to the collapsed rail; expanded rails may reveal secondary destinations.

evidence.result: The rail specimen renders six destinations, within the stated 3–7 range.

implementation.notes: The current specimen count satisfies the explicit allowed range; optional FAB is separately configured.

checks.statement: M3 Expressive introduces collapsed and expanded navigation rails.
checks.condition: When exposing design-generation availability for navigation rail variants.

evidence.result: The navigation specimen exposes collapsed/baseline and expanded cases; the case variant sets collapsed vertical versus expanded horizontal orientation.

implementation.notes: Both collapsed and expanded rail render paths exist in the component specimen.

checks.statement: The baseline navigation rail is no longer recommended; use the collapsed rail instead.
checks.condition: When choosing a rail configuration under M3 Expressive.

evidence.result: The standalone specimen has no app-level integration context for this exact condition: “When choosing a rail configuration under M3 Expressive.”.

implementation.notes: The source says “The baseline navigation rail is no longer recommended; use the collapsed rail instead.” under “When choosing a rail configuration under M3 Expressive.”. This condition concerns destination hierarchy, app layout, product choice, or a screen transition that the isolated navigation-rail specimen does not own. This disposition applies only to that integration condition.

checks.statement: The expanded navigation rail replaces the navigation drawer.
checks.condition: When choosing the corresponding M3 Expressive navigation component.

evidence.result: The standalone specimen has no app-level integration context for this exact condition: “When choosing the corresponding M3 Expressive navigation component.”.

implementation.notes: The source says “The expanded navigation rail replaces the navigation drawer.” under “When choosing the corresponding M3 Expressive navigation component.”. This condition concerns destination hierarchy, app layout, product choice, or a screen transition that the isolated navigation-rail specimen does not own. checks.statement: Collapsed and expanded rails are available in M3 Expressive; the baseline rail is available in M3 and not recommended in M3 Expressive.
checks.condition: When presenting variant availability and recommendation metadata.
checks.notes: Read the complete variant table with the M3 and M3 Expressive column headers; -- denotes no listed availability.

evidence.result: The specimen renders baseline and expressive variants, but does not associate them with M3 versus M3 Expressive generation metadata; upstream availability cannot be inferred from the visible component choices.

implementation.notes: Variant display is present but generation-specific availability/recommendation mapping is absent.

checks.statement: The expanded rail supports standard (default) and modal layouts; M3 provides their predecessors as navigation drawers.
checks.condition: When exposing expanded layout configurations and generation availability.

evidence.result: The preview exposes standard/modal expanded layouts, but the combined source statement also maps their M3 predecessors to navigation drawers; this preview does not encode that generation crosswalk.

implementation.notes: The web preview supports layout modes but does not expose the source design-generation mapping.

checks.statement: Hide when collapsed is an M3 Expressive expanded-rail behavior.
checks.condition: When exposing expanded behavior configurations.

evidence.result: The collapse preview supports collapsed-rail and hidden modes; syncRail hides the navigation surface only when the rail is collapsed and hide mode is selected.

implementation.notes: The behavior is explicitly limited to the expanded-rail layout state and the specimen control offers the configuration.

checks.statement: A collapsed or expanded rail destination contains an icon, active indicator and label; menu, FAB or extended FAB and badges are optional.
checks.condition: When composing an M3 Expressive rail.
checks.notes: Element list and diagram identify anatomy; detailed indicator and badge behavior is captured separately.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated from the captured section and visually inspected diagram.

evidence.result: The rail item has icon, indicator and visible label; optional menu, FAB/extended FAB and badge render paths are present.

implementation.notes: The specimen implements the required destination anatomy and demonstrates optional controls/badges.

checks.statement: Use surface-container for the optional container, on-secondary-container for the active icon, secondary-container for the active indicator, secondary for the vertical active label, on-secondary-container for the horizontal active label, on-surface-variant for inactive icons and labels, error for badges and on-error for badge text.
checks.condition: When mapping collapsed and expanded rail colors in light and dark schemes.
checks.notes: Read the numbered diagram together with its nine color-role entries. FAB colors belong to the FAB component.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated from the captured section and visually inspected diagram.

evidence.result: Generator maps rail state and role tokens to component custom properties; CSS applies active icon/indicator/label, inactive icon/label and error badge bindings, with horizontal labels using the active on-container icon color.

implementation.notes: The renderer binds the stated component roles through the Material token mapping. The optional container and theme values are supplied by generated tokens.

checks.statement: The navigation item target area always spans the full rail width even when the visible item container hugs its content.
checks.condition: For collapsed and expanded rail destinations.

evidence.result: Each navigation item has inline-size:100% within the rail item list; the indicator can independently hug content.

implementation.notes: The interactive button target spans the rail width even when its indicator is narrower.

checks.statement: Represent enabled, hovered, focused and pressed states for navigation destinations.
checks.condition: When rendering collapsed and expanded rail items.
checks.notes: State diagrams show overlays for hovered, focused and pressed items; selection remains visible independently.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated from the captured section and visually inspected diagram.

evidence.result: Navigation item styles define hover, focus-visible and pressed state layers; the native button provides enabled state.

implementation.notes: The state styling covers the four listed interaction states.

checks.statement: Use a 96dp collapsed rail and a 220–360dp expanded rail.
checks.condition: At the default text scale for M3 Expressive rails.
checks.notes: Visually read the width callouts in the captured section’s measurement diagram; dp is a design measurement, mapped to CSS px by the web implementation.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated from the captured section and visually inspected diagram.

evidence.result: The component consumes generated navigation measurement variables, but the immutable assessment copy does not expose resolved values for this measurement.

implementation.notes: The source defines nominal dp measurements; CSS consumes generated token custom properties, but the frozen baseline generated token stylesheet exposing the resolved values is not present in this assessment archive.

checks.statement: Use a 56dp expanded active indicator height, a 36dp rail-edge-to-indicator inset and a 16dp indicator-edge-to-icon inset.

checks.statement: Use 12dp above and 8dp below an expanded section header.
checks.condition: When a section header groups expanded navigation destinations.
checks.notes: Visually read the two section-header callouts in the measurement diagram.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated from the captured section and visually inspected diagram.

evidence.result: Expanded section headers use margin-block start space150 and end space100, corresponding to the source’s 12dp above and 8dp below tokens.

implementation.notes: The header spacing is explicitly tokenized to the requested 12dp/8dp rhythm.

checks.statement: Use an 8dp gap between the destination icon and label.
checks.condition: For the collapsed vertical destination layout at default text scale.
checks.notes: Visually read the 8 callout between icon and label in the measurement diagram.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated from the captured section and visually inspected diagram.

evidence.result: The component consumes generated navigation measurement variables, but the immutable assessment copy does not expose resolved values for this measurement.

implementation.notes: The gap is token-bound in the component CSS, but the exact resolved value cannot be confirmed from this frozen source archive.

checks.statement: Use on-secondary-container for the active icon, secondary-container for its indicator, on-surface for the active label, on-surface-variant for inactive icons and labels, error for badges and on-error for badge text.
checks.condition: When mapping baseline navigation rail colors.
checks.notes: Read the baseline numbered color diagram with its eight role entries.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated from the captured section and visually inspected diagram.

evidence.result: Baseline active icon and indicator, active label, inactive icon/label and badge colors are bound to nav state tokens.

implementation.notes: The renderer maps the baseline roles to the corresponding current/active and inactive token variables.

checks.statement: Represent enabled, hovered, focused and pressed states for both active and inactive destinations.
checks.condition: When rendering the baseline rail.
checks.notes: Visually inspected the eight-state diagram.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated from the captured section and visually inspected diagram.

evidence.result: The shared navigation item stylesheet covers hover, focus-visible and pressed state layers; native destination buttons are enabled by default.

implementation.notes: The CSS state selectors apply to baseline and expressive rail items.

checks.statement: Use an 80dp baseline rail, 24dp icons, a 56×32dp active indicator and 56dp destination height.
checks.condition: At the baseline rail’s default text scale.
checks.notes: Visually read the size-measurement diagram, not the Expressive diagram.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated from the captured section and visually inspected diagram.

evidence.result: The implementation uses token variables for these measurements, but exact values cannot be validated from the available frozen baseline files.

implementation.notes: The baseline rail and item dimensions are sourced from generated component variables; the frozen assessment archive lacks the resolved token stylesheet needed to confirm the stated 80dp/24dp/56×32dp/56dp measurements.

checks.statement: Use 12dp horizontal indicator margins, 4dp between icon and label, and 12dp between destination areas.
checks.condition: At the baseline rail’s default text scale.
checks.notes: Visually read the separate baseline padding-and-margin diagram.

sourceHistory.summary: Curated from the captured section and visually inspected diagram.

evidence.result: The implementation uses token variables for these measurements, but exact values cannot be validated from the available frozen baseline files.

implementation.notes: The indicator margins and item spacing are mapped to measurement variables, but resolved values are unavailable in the frozen source copy.

checks.statement: The menu button transitions between collapsed and expanded rails.
checks.condition: When a menu button is included.

evidence.result: Chromium component-only motion harness at http://127.0.0.1:8082/assessment-motion.html passed 233 assertions; this included navigation-rail LTR/RTL transition geometry and menu state transitions.

implementation.notes: The inspected menu-trigger path switches variant/orientation, moves focus, animates geometry and restores state. Harness omitted the unrelated asset-navigation setup and obsolete Hero DOM group; it passed the component-only rail assertions.

checks.statement: The collapsed navigation rail should not be hidden.
checks.condition: When the collapsed rail is the selected navigation pattern.

evidence.result: The surface is hidden only when the selected collapse mode is hidden; the collapsed-rail mode leaves the surface visible and scrollable.

implementation.notes: The default collapsed-rail behavior keeps the rail shown.

checks.statement: Compact windows should use a navigation bar instead of a standard rail.
checks.condition: When choosing persistent navigation for compact windows.
checks.notes: Expanded modal rails can still open from menu buttons on mobile; do not treat this as a ban on modal expansion.

evidence.result: The standalone specimen has no app-level integration context for this exact condition: “When choosing persistent navigation for compact windows.”.

implementation.notes: The source says “Compact windows should use a navigation bar instead of a standard rail.” under “When choosing persistent navigation for compact windows.”. This condition concerns destination hierarchy, app layout, product choice, or a screen transition that the isolated navigation-rail specimen does not own. This disposition applies only to that integration condition.

checks.statement: A navigation rail should be the only visible primary navigation element.
checks.condition: When using a rail; tabs may provide a separate navigation level.

evidence.result: The standalone specimen has no app-level integration context for this exact condition: “When using a rail; tabs may provide a separate navigation level.”.

implementation.notes: The source says “A navigation rail should be the only visible primary navigation element.” under “When using a rail; tabs may provide a separate navigation level.”. checks.statement: Consider a navigation bar in medium windows with few destinations.
checks.condition: When choosing navigation for a medium window.
checks.notes: This conflicts with Resizing’s “Only use navigation rails for medium breakpoints and larger. Don’t use a navigation bar.” Preserve both instructions until resolved.

evidence.result: The standalone specimen has no app-level integration context for this exact condition: “When choosing navigation for a medium window.”.

implementation.notes: The source says “Consider a navigation bar in medium windows with few destinations.” under “When choosing navigation for a medium window.”. checks.statement: An expanded navigation rail should open from a menu icon.
checks.condition: When opening standard or modal expanded navigation.

evidence.result: The menu icon button carries data-navigation-expand and the click handler toggles between collapsed and expanded variants.

implementation.notes: Both standard and modal expanded rail states use the visible menu control.

checks.statement: An expanded rail may reveal secondary destinations that are not visible when collapsed.
checks.condition: When additional destinations are needed.

evidence.result: The specimen marks Archive and Trash as secondary destinations; CSS hides these entries and their section label while collapsed.

implementation.notes: The expanded state reveals secondary destinations that are hidden in collapsed mode.

checks.statement: Place the standard expanded rail beside body content and the modal expanded rail over body content.
checks.condition: When choosing expanded rail modality.

evidence.result: Standard expanded rail occupies its adjacent slot; modal mode positions the rail surface over content and shows a scrim.

implementation.notes: The layout selector produces side-by-side standard and overlay modal placement.

checks.statement: Use a modal expanded rail for information-dense layouts with limited space or products with many navigation items.
checks.condition: When choosing standard versus modal expanded navigation.

evidence.result: The standalone specimen has no app-level integration context for this exact condition: “When choosing standard versus modal expanded navigation.”.

implementation.notes: The source says “Use a modal expanded rail for information-dense layouts with limited space or products with many navigation items.” under “When choosing standard versus modal expanded navigation.”. This condition concerns destination hierarchy, app layout, product choice, or a screen transition that the isolated navigation-rail specimen does not own. This disposition applies only to that integration condition.

checks.statement: The expanded rail may be hidden in immersive experiences and appear when the menu icon is selected.
checks.condition: When using hide-when-collapsed expanded behavior; the menu icon must remain accessible.

evidence.result: In hidden mode the rail surface is hidden while the external menu control remains exposed; selecting the menu expands the rail.

implementation.notes: The specimen preserves an accessible opener outside the hidden rail.

checks.statement: When the container fill is turned off, all rail items must retain at least 3:1 color contrast.
checks.condition: When rendering the rail directly on the surrounding surface.

evidence.result: The renderer maps active and inactive text/icon colors to Material roles, but no code enforces a 3:1 threshold when the rail container is transparent; the supplied browser harness tested only horizontal selected-label contrast.

implementation.notes: The exact transparent-container condition and all rail item states were not covered by the harness. Token role mapping is present, but the contrast threshold remains unverified.

checks.statement: The navigation rail should run vertically along the side of a layout; use a navigation bar for horizontal navigation.
checks.condition: When placing a rail in a page layout.

evidence.result: Collapsed rail cases set vertical orientation and use column items with vertical icon-label placement; expanded cases set horizontal orientation for their expanded variant.

implementation.notes: The rail layout is vertically arranged as the side navigation pattern, with the expanded horizontal item variant supported separately.

checks.statement: Rail destinations may be top- or center-aligned as a group; use center alignment on tablets.
checks.condition: When positioning the destination group for reachability.

evidence.result: The specimen exposes top/center alignment; center mode applies automatic block margins to the destination group.

implementation.notes: The choice is configurable in the preview, so the alignment behavior is available; tablet recommendation is app policy.

checks.statement: The menu icon and FAB should always be top-aligned.
checks.condition: When either optional control is present.

evidence.result: The optional menu/FAB controls render in the rail header before the destination list; the header is a non-growing flex column.

implementation.notes: Optional controls remain above the destination group.

checks.statement: The menu icon should change to indicate that the expanded rail can be collapsed.
checks.condition: When the rail is expanded.

evidence.result: The menu and collapse glyphs occupy one slot; expanded state changes aria-label and CSS crossfades/rotates to the collapse icon.

implementation.notes: The expanded control communicates and visually shows the collapse action.

checks.statement: A FAB nested in the navigation rail should have resting elevation level 0.
checks.condition: When an optional FAB is present.

evidence.result: A FAB nested in the rail sets its elevation level to system level 0.

implementation.notes: The rail-specific FAB rule sets the required resting elevation token.

checks.statement: Avoid placing the FAB below navigation destinations.
checks.condition: When an optional FAB is present.

evidence.result: Optional FAB renders inside the rail header before the navigation item list.

implementation.notes: The specimen places the FAB before the destinations.

checks.statement: Do not use a logo as the menu button for expanding the rail, and avoid logos that resemble actions or destinations.
checks.condition: When displaying branding at the top of the rail.

evidence.result: The rail expansion control renders the Material menu/menu_open glyph, not a brand logo.

implementation.notes: The menu action is represented with a recognizable menu icon.

checks.statement: Use an active indicator only for the current open page, on no more than one destination at a time.
checks.condition: When displaying navigation selection.

evidence.result: Selection clears aria-current from every destination and sets it only on the clicked button; the active indicator selector is tied to aria-current.

implementation.notes: At most one item receives the current-page state and visible indicator.

checks.statement: The expanded active indicator hugs the label and icon; it may be overridden to fill the container to resemble the baseline navigation drawer.
checks.condition: When sizing the visible expanded active indicator; the target remains full width.

evidence.result: The default indicator width is based on its contents; an explicit data-indicator=fill selector expands it to the full item width.

implementation.notes: The component offers both hugging and full-width override while retaining a full-width target.

checks.statement: Navigation items must use icons that symbolize their destination’s content.
checks.condition: When choosing destination icons.

evidence.result: The standalone specimen has no app-level integration context for this exact condition: “When choosing destination icons.”.

implementation.notes: The source says “Navigation items must use icons that symbolize their destination’s content.” under “When choosing destination icons.”. This condition concerns destination hierarchy, app layout, product choice, or a screen transition that the isolated navigation-rail specimen does not own. This disposition applies only to that integration condition.

checks.statement: A selected icon becomes filled and changes color, with an active indicator behind it.
checks.condition: When selecting a navigation destination.

evidence.result: Both outline and filled glyphs are rendered; aria-current swaps visibility and token styles the selected icon.

implementation.notes: Selection uses filled icon styling and the active indicator.

checks.statement: All navigation items require a short, meaningful one-word label describing the destination.
checks.condition: When authoring destination labels.
checks.notes: The same section permits line breaks or hyphenation when longer labels are unavoidable; retain that exception.

evidence.result: Every destination renders short, one-word visible labels such as Home, Files, Saved and Recent.

implementation.notes: The sample provides concise meaningful labels for each item.

checks.statement: Avoid wrapping long labels where possible; if necessary, break between words or hyphenate longer words.
checks.condition: When a destination label cannot fit on one line.

evidence.result: Rail labels set overflow-wrap:anywhere, which can break within words rather than preferring word boundaries or hyphenation; the specimen has no hyphenation rule.

implementation.notes: The current wrap rule permits arbitrary word breaks and does not implement the source’s preferred between-word/hyphenated behavior.

checks.statement: Do not shrink label text or replace it with an ellipsis to fit more characters.
checks.condition: At default text size; accessibility guidance separately allows truncation beyond 2× scaling.

evidence.result: Rail labels can wrap and measured label height contributes to item block-size; there is no font shrinking or ellipsis rule.

implementation.notes: The style grows item height for label content and does not shrink or ellipsize labels.

checks.statement: Place a collapsed rail’s badge at the icon’s upper right; an expanded rail’s badge should sit next to the label.
checks.condition: When showing count or status badges.
checks.notes: The prose says compact nav rails; interpret this as collapsed rail layout, not the compact window class.

evidence.result: Collapsed vertical badges are positioned at the upper-right of the indicator/icon; expanded horizontal badges remain after the label in the flex item.

implementation.notes: The template places the badge after the label and CSS moves the collapsed case to the icon corner.

checks.notes: The linked transition-pattern page has not been captured in this run; detailed page-transition timing remains outside this check.

evidence.result: The selected state swaps the icon and demo text immediately. No animation of the active indicator expanding from the icon center or app-route transition is present; route transition is outside this isolated preview.

implementation.notes: The selection visuals are implemented, but the check combines an app-level top-level page transition with an indicator animation. The component has no route lifecycle, and the indicator animation requirement is not independently resolved.

checks.statement: Predictive back applies only to the modal expanded rail and reveals the previous screen in a preview.
checks.condition: On Android with predictive back.
checks.notes: This platform-specific rule is not automatically a web requirement; applicability must be assessed separately.

evidence.result: This check is explicitly conditional on Android predictive back and a modal expanded rail; the web implementation has no Android system back gesture or preview API.

implementation.notes: The platform-specific predictive-back behavior cannot apply to the web specimen; no web behavior is inferred from it.

checks.statement: People using assistive technology should be able to navigate destinations, select a destination and receive feedback appropriate to their input.
checks.condition: When interacting with the rail through assistive technology.

evidence.result: The rail is a named nav landmark containing native buttons; selection updates current-page state and a polite output, while the shared key handler supports directional movement.

implementation.notes: The specimen provides semantic navigation, selection feedback and keyboard operation.

checks.statement: On selection, show the active indicator with a ripple, switch the icon from outlined to filled, and change icon and text color.
checks.condition: When tapping a navigation item.

evidence.result: Selection updates aria-current, switches outlined glyphs to filled glyphs and applies active icon/label/indicator tokens. The shared feedback handler recognizes .md-nav-item and appends animated ripple ink to its .md-nav-indicator; ripple markup is created at activation rather than authored in the template. This is code-supported behavior, not full browser verification of selection feedback.

checks.statement: Show a hover state to signal that a destination is interactive.
checks.condition: When hovering a destination with a cursor.

evidence.result: Hover selectors apply a state layer to navigation items when the pointer is not touch; the shared component button behavior handles pointer feedback.

implementation.notes: A cursor hover state is present for interactive destinations.

checks.statement: Active and inactive icon colors need sufficient contrast against the container; do not use low-contrast colors or more than two destination colors.
checks.condition: When choosing rail destination colors.
checks.notes: The section recommends the default scheme. The explicit 3:1 threshold for transparent containers is recorded separately; do not invent a new numeric threshold here.

evidence.result: Active and inactive destination colors are token-mapped, but the check also limits total colors and requires contrast against the container; the browser harness did not exercise every active/inactive color context or the two-color limit.

implementation.notes: The harness result cannot establish this combined requirement. Keep the token role mapping visible while leaving full contrast and color-count conformance unresolved.

checks.statement: Use semibold icon weight for an active destination when its icon has no filled style.
checks.condition: When the icon family lacks a filled variant.

evidence.result: The demonstrated navigation icon family has both outlined and filled SVG glyphs, so the source fallback for icon families without a filled style is not exercised by this specimen.

implementation.notes: The unmet condition is “when the icon family lacks a filled variant”; this specimen supplies both variants.

checks.statement: Navigation items should grow vertically for larger text while retaining default padding; scaled labels may wrap.
checks.condition: When a device increases text size.

evidence.result: A ResizeObserver measures destination label height and updates a CSS variable; vertical item height is max of the token height and indicator, label gap/height and vertical padding.

implementation.notes: The item can grow vertically as labels wrap at larger text sizes while retaining tokenized padding.

checks.statement: Keep the full destination label visible up to 2× text size; beyond that size it may truncate.
checks.condition: When testing device text scaling.

evidence.result: The label is not line-clamped or ellipsized; a ResizeObserver measures its full height and the item grows to contain the label.

implementation.notes: The implementation keeps full text visible through wrapping; no truncation threshold is encoded, so labels also remain untruncated beyond 2×.

checks.statement: Initial focus lands on the first interactive item: the menu, FAB or first destination.
checks.condition: When keyboard focus enters the rail; this does not require stealing focus on page load.

evidence.result: Native focus order starts with the rendered menu/FAB controls and then destination buttons; no focus is moved on page load.

implementation.notes: The first focusable rail action matches the configured menu, FAB or first destination order without stealing focus.

checks.statement: Tab moves from the FAB or menu into the navigation items.
checks.condition: When keyboard focus is on a leading rail control.

evidence.result: The optional header buttons precede the destination buttons in DOM order, so Tab advances from menu/FAB into destinations.

implementation.notes: Sequential keyboard focus follows the required control-to-destination order.

checks.statement: Use a filled selected icon and outlined inactive icons rather than the same unfilled style for both.
checks.condition: When the icon family has filled and outlined styles.

evidence.result: The template supplies outline and filled icon glyphs; the aria-current selector hides outline and shows filled only for the selected destination.

implementation.notes: The selected and inactive icon appearances are distinct.

checks.statement: Tab and arrow keys navigate interactive elements.
checks.condition: When using keyboard navigation within the rail.

evidence.result: Destination traversal filters layout-hidden, visibility-hidden, disabled and inert controls before passing the visible sequence to the existing orientation/RTL index helper. A target outside that sequence does not consume the key.

checks.statement: Space and Enter select the focused interactive element.
checks.condition: When activating a rail destination with the keyboard.

evidence.result: Destination controls are native buttons; Space/Enter produce click activation, which updates aria-current, dispatches the selection event and dismisses modal/expanded navigation as applicable.

implementation.notes: Native button activation is handled by the common click selection path.

checks.statement: The accessible name typically matches the visible label; use a more descriptive accessible name when the visible label is ambiguous.
checks.condition: When naming navigation destinations for assistive technology.
checks.notes: For example, Recent can be named Recent images. The section notes that Android Views lacks this customization and does not announce the role; do not apply that platform limitation to web.

evidence.result: Navigation item buttons have visible text labels, while the named nav landmark describes the group; the button’s accessible name derives from its label text.

implementation.notes: The web specimen uses the visible destination label as the accessible name. More descriptive app-specific names remain available only if surrounding content needs them.
